A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POFUL and course-correction study. Their text, equations, figures, algorithms, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices and the main text.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations on three synthetic bandit problems, with cumulative-regret curves in Figure 2 and 20 independent runs per example.

after.justification: v2 reports the retained synthetic simulations and new experiments on Cardiotocography, JapaneseVowels, and Segment in Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes its stated iteration range from t=1,...,T to t=0,...,T without corresponding initialization changes. Otherwise, POFUL's pivot selection, action rule, and updates remain unchanged, as does Algorithm 2's TS-MR/Greedy-MR switching procedure. The PDFs do not establish an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates three synthetic settings. v2 retains them and adds classification-derived contextual-bandit evaluations using Cardiotocography, JapaneseVowels, and Segment, substantially extending coverage to real datasets.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons evaluate TS-MR and Greedy-MR against LinTS, TS-Freq, OFUL, and Greedy in both versions. Figure 4 extends this same comparator set to the new datasets.

E3.justification: Section 8.2 adds an evaluation protocol that treats classes as actions and gives rewards of 1 for correct classification and 0 otherwise, plus Gaussian noise. The retained synthetic examples preserve their dimensions, action constructions, thresholds, and plotted horizons; their repetition changes are assessed under E5.

E4.justification: The analysis questions remain unchanged, including Example 3's prior-mean-mismatch failure scenario. The added real-data experiments are benchmark comparisons, without new ablations, sensitivity sweeps, distribution-shift tests, or error analyses.

E5.justification: Each retained synthetic example explicitly increases from 20 to 100 independent runs. The new real-data results average 100 duplicates. Shaded bands already appear in v1; v2 does not introduce an explicit confidence-interval definition or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds regret trajectories on three real datasets, showing both course-corrected methods below OFUL and TS-Freq. Synthetic estimates also change with the increased repetition count: for example, Greedy's plotted regret at time 2500 in Example 2 changes from approximately 5500 to 4700. The main synthetic rankings and failure-case conclusions remain.

T1.justification: v2 removes the covering-radius extension comprising v1's Definition 6, Theorem 3, Proposition 6, and Appendix D.5 proof. It also removes Assumption 4, rewrites Lemma 3's proof using eigenvalue multiplicities, and adds Remark 3's action-dependent bound. These materially revise theoretical scope and reasoning. Some inconsistencies remain: Lemma 3 still states distinct eigenvalues, and the new Section 5 inequality reverses the direction implied by its nonpositive optimism term.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: computable instance-dependent POFUL regret bounds and minimax-rate course-corrected LinTS/Greedy variants that preserve desirable empirical and computational properties.

C2.justification: Remark 3 newly explains why course correction needs a bound available before selecting the action. Remark 4 adds guidance linking the threshold to failure risk, exploration, and computational cost. Section 5 also adds a rationale for zero optimism, while Section 8.2 interprets the new results through conservative versus economical exploration.

D1.justification: v2 identifies OpenML as the source of the added datasets and documents their class-to-action and noisy-reward construction. Remark 4 adds qualitative threshold-selection guidance. Preprocessing, noise variance, and dataset-specific threshold values remain unspecified for the new experiments.

R1.justification: The Reznikov and Saff covering-radius citation and reference disappear with the associated theoretical extension. The remaining related-work positioning is substantially unchanged; the updated Kannan et al. publication information concerns the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the central narrative: discrete-action analysis moves from Appendix A to Section 5.1, the proof sketch becomes Section 6, and course correction receives Section 7 with its pseudocode. Experiments split into synthetic and real-data subsections. Explanations are extensively expanded, and sensitivity ratio/regret ratio become uncertainty ratio/regret proxy.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel real-data Figure 4, enlarges the geometric illustrations, and expands their captions. The proof illustration and Algorithm 2 move into the main text. The retained synthetic comparison keeps its three-panel organization and comparator legends.

improvement.justification: The new real-data comparisons and 100-run synthetic averages strengthen empirical support, while the reorganized calibration and proof material improves accessibility. These gains are tempered by the removed covering-radius extension, incomplete settings for the new experiments, and the newly reversed inequality in Section 5. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement rather than an unqualified theoretical strengthening.
